key_insight: A multimodal graph neural network can integrate heterogeneous biomedical data to identify and prioritize cancer immunotherapy targets, and top predictions are validated in clinically relevant patient-derived tumour explants.
problem_solved: Addresses the challenge of systematically discovering and ranking clinically relevant immunotherapy targets from diverse molecular and clinical datasets, while providing translational validation in a patient-derived platform to increase confidence in predictions.
method: Build a multimodal graph that links genes/proteins, pathways, cell types and patient features and train a graph neural network to score candidate targets.
Classify and prioritize targets (approved, prospective, novel) based on learned embeddings and predictive scores.
Experimentally validate top-ranked candidates using a patient-derived tumour explant (PDTE) platform to confirm immune-modulatory activity and translational relevance.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical workflow for combining heterogeneous biomedical data with GNNs for drug-target discovery and demonstrates the value of coupling computational predictions with clinically relevant experimental validation to accelerate translational impact.
visual_elements: Schematic of the multimodal graph (nodes: genes/proteins, patients, pathways; edges: interactions/associations)
Pipeline flowchart: data integration → GNN model → target ranking → PDTE validation
Comparison chart showing model performance and how it separates approved vs prospective/novel targets
Illustrative icon set showing prediction → patient-derived tissue assay → validated candidate
paper_title: Immunotherapy drug target identification using machine learning and patient-derived tumour explant validation
paper_authors: Marcellus Augustine, Nuno Rocha Nene, Hongchang Fu, Christopher L. Pinder, Lorena Ligammari
